title: Response Compression: Smaller Responses With Gzip and Brotli | Orchard Core
description:
Pages, stylesheets, scripts and JSON responses are text, and text compresses well, but a tenant sends it uncompressed until something compresses it.

The Response Compression module adds the ASP.NET Core response compression middleware to a tenant. You enable one feature, and the tenant compresses the responses that clients accept compressed.

In this video:
• How compression works: Accept-Encoding and Content-Encoding
• Enable the feature in Tools, Features
• Enable it in a recipe with the Feature step
• Inside the module: services, middleware and order
• Check the result with a request that accepts one format
• When to use it: a proxy first, and the HTTPS risk
